label: Van Buren Withdraws From Race
detail: The Free Soil nominee leaves the race before election day, so antislavery voters must choose between the two major nominees or stay home.
assumption: The third-party candidate is removed from the ballot; his voters are reallocated among the two major nominees and abstention, with antislavery Northern voters more likely to leave the major party they broke from.
facts_text: The nominee of a new coalition of antislavery breakaways from both major parties and the old antislavery party, pledged to keep slavery out of all the territories, announced in the autumn that he is leaving the contest.
His name will not be presented to voters by the coalition's electors, and its leaders have left supporters to decide for themselves how to vote.
research_questions: Where third-party candidates withdrew before an election, how did their supporters split between the major parties and abstention?
How did former Democratic Barnburners in New York behave when their preferred faction had no candidate?
How did antislavery Whigs react when a Free Soil option was unavailable?
source_text: Martin Van Buren doesn't run as the Free Soil candidate in 1848.
